title: Risk controls and safe movement
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Explain and apply: risk controls and safe movement

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Overview
instruction.body: In this lesson, practise risk controls and safe movement using an authorised work order and a realistic Australian cleaning-site scenario. Work only within training, employer procedures and site-specific instructions.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body: Prefer eliminating hazards over relying solely on PPE. Use warning signs, barriers and safe lifting methods; do not move loads or work at heights beyond approved procedures.

instruction.heading: Choose effective controls
instruction.body: Where practicable eliminate the hazard or substitute a safer method before relying on signs or PPE. For a wet walkway, close access and dry it rather than relying only on a warning sign.

instruction.heading: Move and handle safely
instruction.body: Plan carrying routes, reduce load size, use carts on suitable ground and request assistance for awkward loads. Avoid twisting while lifting; stop when the load or route is beyond safe capability.

instruction.heading: Protect other people
instruction.body: Keep cables away from walkways, mark work zones, never obstruct exits and maintain separation from the public. Select PPE to suit the task and instructions, not as a replacement for other controls.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

procedure: Consider whether the hazard can be eliminated or substituted before relying on warning signs or PPE.
Close access and dry a wet walkway where practicable, rather than relying on a warning sign alone.
Plan the carrying route and reduce the size of the load before lifting.
Use a cart on suitable ground, and ask for help with awkward loads.
Avoid twisting while lifting, and stop when the load or route is beyond your safe capability.
Keep cables off walkways, mark work zones, and keep exits clear.
Select PPE to suit the task and the instructions, and do not use it in place of other controls.
Work only within approved procedures, and stop and tell your supervisor before resuming if the work falls outside them.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

qualityStandard: Elimination or substitution of the hazard is considered before warning signs or PPE are used.
Carrying routes are planned, loads are reduced where possible, and the cleaner stops when a load or route is beyond safe capability.
Cables are kept off walkways, work zones are marked, and exits are never obstructed.
PPE is selected to suit the task and does not replace other controls.
summary: Hazards are eliminated or substituted where practicable before signs or PPE are relied on.
Loads are moved along planned routes, with smaller loads, suitable carts and help for awkward items, and no work goes beyond approved procedures.
Other people are protected by keeping cables off walkways, marking work zones, keeping exits clear and staying separated from the public.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is a warning sign alone often insufficient for a wet walkway?
options: Because a sign is a substitute for drying the floor or restricting access
Because people read signs before they walk on wet floors and the sign is always visible
Because a sign does not remove the hazard. Close access and dry the floor where practicable
Because the wet floor can be walked on safely once the sign is up and the sign is always visible

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do if a required control or instruction is unavailable?
options: Stop and get the required control or instruction before proceeding
Use the nearest substitute and record it later
Work faster to finish before the control is needed
Improvise a barrier from a spare chair and a roll of tape
